ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the image is the larger triangle QTP, with vertex P at the upper left, T at the lower left, and Q in the middle on the right; side QP is marked as 11, side QT is marked as 15, and side PT is marked as 16. On the right side is the smaller triangle QRS, with vertex Q on the left, R at the upper right, and S at the lower right; side QR is marked as 5. Reasoning: It is known that triangle QRS ~ triangle QTP, so the corresponding vertices are Q ↔ Q, R ↔ T, S ↔ P. Therefore QR corresponds to QT, QS corresponds to QP, and RS corresponds to TP. The similarity ratio from the large triangle QTP to the small triangle QRS is QR/QT = 5/15 = 1/3. Thus QS = 11/3, RS = 16/3. The perimeter of the small triangle QRS is QR + QS + RS = 5 + 11/3 + 16/3 = 5 + 27/3 = 5 + 9 = 14.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram: triangle QTP has side lengths QP = 11, QT = 15, and PT = 16, while the corresponding side QR in triangle QRS is labeled 5. From triangle QRS ~ triangle QTP, QR corresponds to QT, so the similarity scale from the large triangle QTP to the small triangle QRS is 5/15 = 1/3. First compute the perimeter of the larger triangle QTP: 11 + 15 + 16 = 42.
